note: Intelligensicus outpost map data. Each feature is one plotted location. Add entries over time; the map reads this file live. track drives the pin color and which species-range layer it belongs to. why = the site rationale shown in the popup. slug = the track proposal it links to. These are ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder points seeded by species geography and master-plan overlap; replace/extend with real sites.

exclusions.title: Davidson Seamount octopus garden
exclusions.why: Rare deep-sea Muusoctopus nursery (MBARI): thousands nesting at warm seeps, multi-year brooding. A unique, sensitive aggregation. AVOIDED, not worked — protected, never a study or box site.

exclusions.title: North Atlantic right whale calving grounds (SE US)
exclusions.why: Critically endangered species with NOAA-designated critical calving habitat off Georgia and Florida. AVOIDED: a fragile calving population, protected, never worked.

exclusions.title: Vaquita refuge, upper Gulf of California
exclusions.why: The vaquita porpoise, the most endangered marine mammal, with fewer than a couple dozen left in a protected refuge. AVOIDED absolutely: conservation-only, never a study site.

exclusions.title: Virunga / Bwindi mountain gorillas (core)
exclusions.why: Critically endangered mountain gorillas in their protected core range. AVOIDED as a hands-on uplift site: observation and conservation only, no scaffolding of a fragile last population.

exclusions.title: Deep-sea egg-brooding aggregations (general class)
exclusions.why: The broader class of rare deep-sea egg-brooding fish and cephalopod aggregations at hydrothermal seeps (like the Davidson garden). AVOIDED wherever found: unique reproductive sites, protected, never boxed.

exclusions.title: Polar bear denning areas (Arctic)
exclusions.why: Polar bears are a conservation-only, climate-crisis species (never an uplift target per the bear plan); maternal denning areas are especially sensitive. AVOIDED entirely.

exclusions.title: Amazon river dolphin (boto) core habitat
exclusions.why: A threatened freshwater cetacean under mounting pressure in its river-system core. AVOIDED as a scaffolding site: too fragile; observation and conservation only.

exclusions.title: Critical nurseries / rare aggregations (general)
exclusions.why: The standing rule, not a single site: the program excludes rare, unique, ecologically sensitive concentrations everywhere, targeting only common, robust populations.

note_schema: flagship sites set flagship:true and carry the three siting variables: nearHotspot (near the species concentration, not on top of it), townResource (a resourced town for teams on long stays; an existing research station or university is a FAVORABLE factor when present, NOT a hard requirement), permitting (the access/permit path, stated honestly incl. heavy state-sanctioned cases). Regular candidate pins omit these; they are the wider field of operable sites shown in All-species view.

outposts.title: Bodega Bay (UC Davis BML)
outposts.why: Northern-California two-spot octopus in the rocky subtidal, anchored to a leading university marine lab.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the rocky-reef octopus population off Bodega Head without sitting on any single aggregation.
outposts.townResource: UC Davis Bodega Marine Laboratory: full research and education facility with on-site housing for long team stays.
outposts.permitting: University field-station pathway: established scientific-collecting permits and an on-hand IACUC host.

outposts.title: Monterey Bay margin (Hopkins / MBARI)
outposts.why: Dense central-coast cephalopod grounds beside the strongest marine-science cluster on the coast.
outposts.nearHotspot: Sited on the accessible bay margin, deliberately NOT in the National Marine Sanctuary core.
outposts.townResource: Monterey: a full town plus Hopkins Marine Station (Stanford, est. 1892), MBARI, and the Aquarium.
outposts.permitting: Sanctuary-adjacent siting keeps the permit path workable; station partnership eases collecting authorization.

outposts.title: Santa Barbara shelf (UCSB)
outposts.why: Rich Channel Islands cephalopod habitat, worked from the mainland shelf next to a marine-science university.
outposts.nearHotspot: On the mainland shelf near the islands, not inside the Channel Islands National Marine Sanctuary.
outposts.townResource: Santa Barbara plus UCSB marine science: town amenities and a university host for extended stays.
outposts.permitting: Mainland-shelf siting avoids the islands' sanctuary core; standard state collecting permits apply.

outposts.title: Catalina (USC Wrigley, Two Harbors)
outposts.why: Warm-shelf octopus at a dedicated island marine station with dive and housing infrastructure.
outposts.nearHotspot: Island-shelf octopus habitat worked from the station side, away from protected reserve cores.
outposts.townResource: USC Wrigley Marine Science Center with dive and lodging support; Two Harbors as a small resource base.
outposts.permitting: University marine-station access, outside the heaviest mainland MPA layering.

outposts.title: La Jolla / San Diego (Scripps)
outposts.why: Southern two-spot range on a warm shelf, anchored to the deepest research-and-city resource base on the coast.
outposts.nearHotspot: Sited near, not inside, the La Jolla reserves and MPAs.
outposts.townResource: San Diego plus Scripps Institution of Oceanography (UCSD): major-city amenities and a top oceanographic host.
outposts.permitting: Reserve-adjacent siting keeps the path clear; Scripps partnership supports collecting authorization.

outposts.title: Half Moon Bay shelf (candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: accessible central-coast rocky shelf between Bodega and Monterey; fills the field of operable sites.

outposts.title: Morro Bay / Central Coast (candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: Central Coast estuary-and-shelf access between Monterey and Santa Barbara.

outposts.title: Florida Keys / Dry Tortugas
outposts.why: Warm shelf octopus habitat; R/V ANGARI charter range already priced (a separate coast, shown for reach).

outposts.title: Mediterranean shelf (Naples)
outposts.why: Octopus vulgaris heartland; the puzzle-box literature's home water.

outposts.title: Seto Inland Sea
outposts.why: High cephalopod density and a strong marine-research culture; overlaps cetacean corridors.

outposts.title: Shark Bay / Monkey Mia (Dolphin Project)
outposts.why: Sponge-tool dolphin culture with maternal-line transmission (Mann 2012), at an established long-term dolphin research station.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the documented Shark Bay dolphin community from the Monkey Mia station, not by pursuing pods offshore.
outposts.townResource: The Shark Bay Dolphin Research Project + Monkey Mia facilities: a standing field station with lodging and boats.
outposts.permitting: Long-running permitted dolphin research program; a proven MMPA-equivalent authorization pathway to build on.

outposts.title: Salish Sea (Friday Harbor Labs)
outposts.why: Well-studied resident orca pods worked wild-only from a world-class marine station.
outposts.nearHotspot: Observes resident orca pods from the San Juan station; wild observation and non-invasive scaffolding only.
outposts.townResource: UW Friday Harbor Laboratories: full marine research facility, housing, and vessels in the pods' range.
outposts.permitting: MMPA scientific-research posture, no captures; the station is an established permit and IACUC host.

outposts.title: Dominica (Project CETI sperm whales)
outposts.why: The sperm-whale study population behind the phonetic-alphabet work (Sharma 2024); acoustic and song-culture focus.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the resident Dominica sperm-whale clan CETI already studies, from port, non-invasively.
outposts.townResource: Roseau and the CETI field presence: a Caribbean port base with an in-place research partnership.
outposts.permitting: Builds on CETI's existing permitted, non-invasive acoustic-research footprint.

outposts.title: Monterey Bay (cetacean, candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: dolphin and whale traffic beside the Monterey marine-science cluster; shares the marine-box coast.

outposts.title: Seattle (Marzluff / UW crow lab)
outposts.why: The proven urban flock behind the face-recognition and social-transmission findings, at the lab that documented them.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works resident city crows in and around the University of Washington campus flock.
outposts.townResource: Seattle plus UW's School of Environmental and Forest Sciences (Marzluff's crow lab): city amenities and a ready host.
outposts.permitting: Migratory-bird research permits only, materially lighter than the marine or near-person regimes.

outposts.title: Tokyo (walnut-cracking crows)
outposts.why: Documented crosswalk nut-cracking innovation; the urban-abundance thesis running in the wild in a major research city.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the large-billed-crow population in the metropolitan wards where the behavior is documented.
outposts.townResource: Tokyo: dense resources and multiple universities for cohorts on long stays.
outposts.permitting: Native-bird research permitting under Japanese wildlife law; no marine or near-person burden.

outposts.title: New Caledonia (tool crows)
outposts.why: New Caledonian crow tool-manufacture, the aviary-cognition heartland the box rigs are built around.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the wild tool-using crow population in its home range, near but not disrupting nesting sites.
outposts.townResource: Noumea as the resource base; an established site for visiting corvid-cognition field teams.
outposts.permitting: Territorial wildlife research permits; a well-trodden path for the existing crow-cognition groups.

outposts.title: Cambridge / Oxford (candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: strong corvid-cognition labs plus resident rook and jackdaw populations in a university city.

outposts.title: Maasai Mara (Sapolsky-line baboons)
outposts.why: The region of Sapolsky's transmitted peaceable-baboon culture (Sapolsky and Share 2004); the origin population for the whole scaffold-a-wild-culture thesis.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works habituated savanna baboon troops of the kind Sapolsky followed for three decades in the greater Mara ecosystem.
outposts.townResource: The Mara has lodges and long-standing field-research presence for extended seasons; a formal host would be arranged, not assumed.
outposts.permitting: HEAVY and honest: the Maasai Mara is a protected, community-and-government-governed reserve. Any hands-on program would require a lofty, state-sanctioned arrangement with Kenyan authorities and Maasai community consent, not a casual field permit. Access, if ever, is a deliberate national-level undertaking.

outposts.title: Amboseli (baboon research, candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: the separate long-running Amboseli baboon research lineage; a protected-park population, distinct from Sapolsky's Mara troop.

outposts.title: Gombe (Goodall chimpanzee culture)
outposts.why: Sixty-plus years of chimpanzee culture research (Whiten 1999 lineage); wild transmission already documented on site.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works the habituated Gombe chimpanzee community that the Stream Research Centre has followed for decades.
outposts.townResource: Gombe Stream Research Centre (Jane Goodall Institute): a standing field station on Lake Tanganyika.
outposts.permitting: Tanzanian research permits + near-person sanctuary ethic + strict two-way disease control, on an established footing.

outposts.title: Amboseli (matriarch knowledge)
outposts.why: Long-term matriarch-knowledge research (McComb); the thesis made literal in a population whose matrilines are already tracked.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works habituated savanna family groups whose matrilines are already individually known.
outposts.townResource: The long-running Amboseli elephant-research presence is a helpful base where it exists; a formal host is arranged, not assumed.
outposts.permitting: Kenyan wildlife and protected-park permits + ESA/CITES for a listed species; conservation-partnership coordination required.

outposts.title: Northern Thailand (sanctuary method-ground)
outposts.why: Asian-elephant sanctuary method-ground paired with wild-range access; the ethical captive lever for the wild work.
outposts.nearHotspot: Pairs an ethical sanctuary method-ground with nearby wild-range populations, never new captures.
outposts.townResource: Chiang Mai plus established ethical elephant sanctuaries and mahout partnerships for long stays.
outposts.permitting: Sanctuary and near-person welfare review + ESA/CITES; mahout-partnership access already exists.

outposts.title: Katmai / Brooks Falls
outposts.why: Habituated, non-food-conditioned brown bears; the ideal observed-wild study access, with the no-food rule already the site norm.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works bears that are naturally feeding and observer-habituated, exactly the no-food-conditioning model.
outposts.townResource: National Park Service infrastructure at Brooks Camp supplies a seasonal field base.
outposts.permitting: NPS and state wildlife-research permits; the park's strict no-feeding rules ALIGN with the track's hard rule.

outposts.title: Great Smoky Mountains (black bear, candidate)
outposts.why: Regular candidate: dense, studied American black-bear population with university partners and a no-feeding culture.

outposts.title: Rust Belt cities (urban rodents)
outposts.why: Urban-rodent abundance as a naturally occurring uplift condition; pairs directly with the corvid urban thesis.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works city rodent and stray-carnivore populations where urban abundance already runs the condition set.
outposts.townResource: Major Midwestern universities and city infrastructure host the paired wild-and-domestic study arms.
outposts.permitting: Light: local wildlife-research permits for the wild arm, companion-animal welfare review for the domestic partner.

outposts.title: Australian rangelands (dingo)
outposts.why: Wild dingo counterpart plus village-dog study partners; the dual-track lever at its clearest.
outposts.nearHotspot: Works wild dingo populations alongside domestic-dog study partners, not captive-only work.
outposts.townResource: Regional research stations and university partners provide the field base for long rangeland seasons.
outposts.permitting: State wildlife-research permits for the dingo arm; companion-animal welfare for the domestic partner.
